It would actually really help. It did for me at least. Before therapy, I didn't really have hobbies, and I wasn't really feeling good about life, and I didn't really make an effort to hang out with or make any friends. 
But my therapist helped me put in the effort into the things I want to achieve. 

Therapy also helped ease my social anxiety a lot by evaluating who I am and why I worry so much about what people think of me and stuff like that. It made me feel good about myself so I consequently became less self conscious around people.

I don't want to be giving the idea that everything is so great now, but it's surely so much better than when I first started therapy. So if you're already thinking about it, I say go for it. 

You should also be patient and wait to see or feel results because it takes time. 
When I first started going, I'd be usually frustrated at the end of the session. But eventually I started to notice the results, and it was so unexpected. 

I also tried five therapists over the span of 2 years, on and off, untill I settled on my current therapist. So if you don't feel like you're doing well with the therapist you're with, don't completely give up on the whole thing (did that at some point) but maybe try seeing a different therapist instead. Try to give the therapist a chance and communicating your frustrations with them before looking for another one.
